Definition: properly, abrupt, i.e. a precipice; by implication, the front; used only adverbially (with prepositional prefix) opposite
BiblicalUsage: n m; 1) front; 1a) front; 1b) in the opposite direction; prep; 2) in front of; 2a) in front of; 2b) (with prefix); 2b1) towards the front of, to the front of, on the front of; 2b2) from the front of, off the front of, close in front of, on the forefront of
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
